If the value of goods you plan to buy is uncertain or seen as short-term, you might be encouraged to convert money into assets that can be later shared—or at least justified in a way that contributes to societal resilience. This could lead to a future where your financial choices are judged not just on value but on perceived importance to the group, blurring the line between personal finance and social responsibility.
